observation_summary: The SimplexSolver produced incorrect optimization results for certain linear programming problems.
reasoning_summary: The bug was caused by an inconsistency in how floating-point values were compared during the Simplex algorithm's execution. Specifically, the algorithm used a strict 'ulp' (unit in the last place) comparison when dropping columns after Phase 1, whereas the convergence check in Phase 1 used an 'epsilon' threshold. This discrepancy caused the algorithm to incorrectly identify columns to drop, leading to incorrect optimization results. The fix involved standardizing the comparison to use the 'epsilon' threshold, ensuring consistency with the convergence logic.
